title: Screening for Intimate Partner Violence Victimisation in Perinatal Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the prevalence of intimate partner violence (IPV) victimisation identified through routine screening in perinatal care and examined which forms of IPV were assessed by the screening tools used. PsycINFO, Medline, Scopus, CINAHL and Embase databases were searched on 16 May 2025. Studies were included if they were peer-reviewed, published in English, and reported the prevalence of IPV victimisation identified using an IPV screening tool administered as part of routine perinatal care. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI’s Critical Appraisal Checklist for Studies Reporting Prevalence Data. Thirteen studies ( n = 614,799) were included in a random-effects meta-analysis. The pooled prevalence of any IPV detected through routine screening in perinatal care was 3.6% (95% CI [2.5, 5.1]). Screening tools used across studies varied considerably, and many lacked psychometric validation. Although most tools assessed physical and psychological IPV, psychological IPV was not comprehensively assessed, with limited coverage of domains beyond emotional abuse, such as control, manipulation and isolation. The pooled prevalence identified through routine screening was lower than estimates reported in the broader perinatal IPV literature, suggesting that current screening practices may underestimate IPV victimisation in perinatal care settings. Greater consistency in screening practices and more comprehensive assessment of IPV domains, particularly psychological and sexual IPV, may improve detection in routine care.
